**Note to manager — FP-1188 / CMM-4471 loading result**

**Bottom line: plate NOT released — one bushing cannot meet tolerance due to a clamp interference. Fixture maintenance needed before tonight's run.**

- K1–K4 and K6 are seated on their markers within 0.09 mm (verified by vision check against the 18:22 plate survey, which I confirmed matches the camera-detected marker positions to ~0.06 mm).
- **K5/M5 fails at 1.03 mm (limit 0.25 mm).** Clamp C2's lip edge sits 9.0 mm from the M5 centre, but the bushing radius is 10 mm — the lip encroaches ~1 mm into the bushing's footprint. Straight-down placement stops against the lip, and nudging cannot pass it; I also verified there is no low-level slide-in path (tool envelope) and that the lip blocks at bushing height, so no approach geometry fixes it.
- I deliberately did **not** touch or loosen clamp C2: it's bolted, and any plate shift would invalidate the 18:22 marker survey that CMM-4471 runs from (the program does not re-measure the markers) — that would have turned a visible failure into silent bad measurements.

**Recommended action:** reposition or re-toe clamp C2 (or fit a slimmer lip), re-survey M1–M6, then reload — K5 is the only bushing that needs placing; the other five are already good. I logged all of this in ~/LOGBOOK.md. Robot time used: 3:19 of 10:00.
